1.explanation: The FluidTextInput component is responsible for rendering the fluid variant of TextInput and PasswordInput, yet it has no implementation for handling a skeleton prop. It never reads a skeleton boolean or conditionally renders any skeleton styling or placeholder components. To fix the missing skeleton state, you need to update FluidTextInput (and possibly its propTypes) to accept a skeleton prop, then wrap or replace the inner TextInput/PasswordInput with the appropriate SkeletonText or SkeletonPlaceholder markup and CSS when skeleton is true.
1.bug_scenario: When a FluidTextInput is rendered with the skeleton prop set to true (e.g. <FluidTextInput skeleton={true} …/>), nothing in the component changes to display the skeleton‐loading UI. According to the design spec screenshots the input border and placeholder (label) should render as gray skeleton bars, but since FluidTextInput simply delegates to TextInput/PasswordInput and never checks for a skeleton prop or applies the SkeletonPlaceholder/SkeletonText components or CSS, no skeleton state is ever shown.

2.explanation: FluidTextInput.js is the core component that needs to support the new skeleton prop. It currently destructures only className, isPassword, and passes all other props down to TextInput/PasswordInput, but doesn’t handle skeleton at all. The FluidTextInput function itself must detect skeleton=true and render the SkeletonText or SkeletonPlaceholder variants instead of the input. The stories file must also expose skeleton in its controls and show the skeleton state. These are the key places where code must change to add, document, and visualize the skeleton state for fluid inputs.
2.bug_scenario: The user is trying to render a fluid text input in its skeleton (loading) state, but nothing changes when passing skeleton={true}. The supplied mockup shows a gray ‘background’ panel with a very light gray horizontal line (label placeholder) above a thicker light gray bar (text‐input placeholder) with a thin darker-gray bottom border. It’s missing entirely in the current FluidTextInput implementation – instead it always renders as a normal TextInput or PasswordInput.
